alex_m: Heads up — CI red on my branch `feature/payment-intent-refactor`. Failing test on linux-py310 matrix.
ci-bot: build failed — job: payment-refactor-linux-py310 #456 — Exit code 1 — see https://ci.redwood/run/456
alex_m: Error is in TestPaymentSession.test_timeout_handling: TimeoutError after 30s. Locally tests pass. I rebased onto main and resolved conflicts yesterday.
sam_g: @alex_m can you paste the failing stack trace?
alex_m: ```
E   TimeoutError: waiting for session timed out
tests/payment/test_session.py:78: TimeoutError
``` 
priya_r: This one flaked for us last week too, usually due to asyncio loop scheduling on CI. Did you bump any timeouts or introduce sleeps?
alex_m: I didn't touch that file. My merge resolved a conflict in payments/__init__.py and updated requirements to stripe==3.2.0.
emma_l: @ci-bot can you rerun job payment-refactor-linux-py310? :eyes: 
ci-bot: rerun requested by emma_l — queued job #457
ravi_k: If it passes locally maybe it's a flaky test. Try reproducing with `pytest tests/payment/test_session.py::TestPaymentSession::test_timeout_handling -q` and `-n 0` to avoid xdist.
sam_g: Also try running inside the CI docker image: `docker run --rm -v $PWD:/work -w /work ci-image:latest pytest tests/payment/test_session.py::TestPaymentSession::test_timeout_handling -q` — env diffs often matter.
alex_m: I reran the job and it failed again. Same trace. I ran the test in docker image and it passed.
priya_r: Could be a dep change — stripe bump might have pulled in a new event loop behaviour? Try pinning stripe back in a local venv.
alex_m: Rolling back stripe to 3.1.8 locally — tests still pass. Not sure.
sam_g: Let's bisect — is there a commit in your branch that could introduce non-determinism? Maybe something touching async fixtures.
alex_m: I can try `git bisect` across my branch. It's ~12 commits since branch creation. Will start in ~1h if nobody beats me to it.
emma_l: I'll queue a full matrix rerun and also mark test as flaky in CI to allow pass-within-retries while we triage. @priya_r can you open a quick flaky-test ticket if we confirm?
priya_r: Yep — will open a ticket if rerun passes then fails consistently.
ci-bot: job #457 finished — PASS
alex_m: job #457 passed on rerun. leaving this open to watch for recurrence. Thanks all :tada: 
sam_g: Follow-up: add a ticket to capture flaky tests and flake rate for that test. If it recurs, we should either increase timeout or make fixture deterministic.
alex_m: filed ticket: https://tracker.redwood/ISSUE-1234 — added logs and reproduce steps.
ci-bot: note: reruns are limited; if flaking becomes frequent we'll need a test fix.
